components.name: SocialPost
components.when_to_use: the video quotes something somebody posted online and the SOURCE is part of the claim — a YouTube comment, a tweet, a Reddit card. `platform` picks the chrome
components.when_not_to_use: a quotation from a book, a speech or an interview, where the words matter and the medium does not (QuoteBlock); a page rather than a post (WebPageFrame); a press headline (HeadlineStack); naming the person without showing what they wrote (NamePlate)

platform.description: which chrome to draw; the shape is the same for all three

handle.description: without the @ or u/ prefix; the component adds the right one

timestamp.description: as the platform would show it: '3 years ago', 'Mar 14'

avatar.description: path to a still under the video dir; omitted draws a monogram disc

components.name: WebPageFrame
components.when_to_use: a web page is the evidence — a filing, an article, a product listing — and the shot has to show both that it is a real page and which part of it matters. `highlight_region` pushes in on that part
components.when_not_to_use: a post rather than a page, where who said it is the point (SocialPost); a photograph or a document image with no browser around it (FramedExhibit, DocumentCard); a press headline (HeadlineStack)

image.description: path to a screenshot under the video dir; omitted draws a wireframe placeholder

highlight_region.description: the part worth reading, as fractions of the image; the shot ends here

components.name: HeadlineStack
components.when_to_use: two to five press headlines land in sequence to show that everyone reported it at once — the montage IS the argument
components.when_not_to_use: the video's own claims in its own voice (BulletList); one headline worth reading in full (FactCard, or DocumentCard for the page itself); something an individual posted (SocialPost); dated events on a rail (Timeline)

items.description: in the order they should land
